question.text:
(a) Define one volt potential difference between two points in an electric field. [1]

parts.label: (a)

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Draw a schematic diagram of an electric circuit of a cell of 1.5 V, 5 Ω and 10 Ω resistor and a plug key, all connected in series. Calculate the current drawn from the cell when the key is closed.

scheme.valuePoint: 1 V: one joule of work done to move one coulomb of charge between the two points (1 V = 1 J/1 C)
Schematic diagram: cell, 5 Ω and 10 Ω resistors, plug key in series

cases.text:
(a) The potential difference between two points is one volt when one joule of work is done to move one coulomb of charge from one point to the other.
1 V = 1 J / 1 C
(b) [Diagram: a rectangular series circuit - a cell (long and short plates) labelled '1.5 V', a zig-zag resistor labelled '5 Ω', a zig-zag resistor labelled '10 Ω', and a plug key drawn as a circle with a dot labelled 'K (plug key)', all in one loop; small arrows show the current direction.]
R = 5 Ω + 10 Ω = 15 Ω

question.text: A solid wooden toy is in the form of a hemisphere surmounted by a cone of the same radius. The radius of hemisphere is 3.5 cm and the total wood used in making the toy is 166 5/6 cm³. Find the height of the conical part. Also, find the cost of painting the hemispherical part of the toy at the rate of ₹ 15 per cm². (Take π = 22/7.)

cases.text:
Let the height of the cone be h cm, r = 3.5 cm.
Volume of toy = volume of cone + volume of hemisphere
166 5/6 = 1/3 πr²h + 2/3 πr³
1001/6 = 1/3 × 22/7 × (3.5)² × h + 2/3 × 22/7 × (3.5)³
1001/6 = 77/6 h + 539/6
1001 = 77h + 539 ⇒ 77h = 462 ⇒ h = 7 cm
CSA of hemisphere = 2πr² = 2 × 22/7 × 3.5 × 3.5 = 77 cm²
Cost of painting = 15 × 77 = ₹ 1155

question.text: Given that √3 is irrational number, prove that (2 + 3√3) is an irrational number.

citation.ref: SQP 2026-27 Maths Standard 041 MS · Q26 · p4
citation.question: Q26

scheme.valuePoint: Since a, b are integers, (a − 2b)/3b is rational

citation.ref: SQP 2026-27 Maths Standard 041 MS · Q26 · p5
citation.question: Q26

scheme.valuePoint: So √3 is rational - contradicts that √3 is irrational; hence the assumption is wrong and 2 + 3√3 is irrational

citation.ref: SQP 2026-27 Maths Standard 041 MS · Q26 · p5
citation.question: Q26

cases.text:
Let us assume that 2 + 3√3 is a rational number.
Then 2 + 3√3 = a/b, where a and b are integers and b ≠ 0.
⇒ 3√3 = a/b − 2 = (a − 2b)/b ⇒ √3 = (a − 2b)/3b
Since a and b are integers, (a − 2b)/3b is rational.
So √3 is rational. But this contradicts the given fact that √3 is irrational.
